text:
Vasily Podkolzin was a tenth overall pick who never quite found a role in Vancouver. In Edmonton he has found one. Daily Faceoff Edmonton is now writing about how he became "one the NHL's best power forwards," and our numbers flag him as one of the league's breakouts.

The role changed first. He is playing 18:06 a night, up from 15:23, and he is on the ice for 46% of the Oilers' power-play time after 12% last season. With it came the production: 14 goals and 23 points in 27 games, a six-game point streak, plus 84 hits. His own chances are up to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.78.

Not all of it will hold. He is shooting 26% against 14% last season, with four more goals than his chances, and the Oilers have scored 11 more goals than expected with him on the ice. We flag him as due to cool. But the chances are real, Edmonton takes 60% of the 5v5 shot attempts in his minutes, and only he and Evan Bouchard sit ahead of McDavid on the club's current iron-man list. He has earned the minutes.
headline: Vasily Podkolzin, Edmonton's breakout power forward
